text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: GPU_MEMORY_PRESSURE_HIGH on gpu-node-12 (us-west-2, inference-pool-prod) — severity: P1. PD incident: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD12345

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty notification: page sent to @oncall-alex, escalation to @sre-maya at +8m if unacked.

oncall-alex: Acked. I'll grab logs and triage. Re-assigning channel to eng-oncall thread.

oncall-alex: Quick look at metrics — node gpu-node-12 memory usage 97%, GPU processes showing persistent allocation from model-serving pod inference-redwood-5. Observed OOMs in dmesg.

oncall-alex: Running initial commands to inspect pods and logs:
```bash
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep gpu-node-12
kubectl -n inference logs inference-redwood-5 --tail=200
# nvml top-like summary (via nvidia-smi)
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY
```

sre-maya: Thanks Alex. If this is continuous allocation we should cordon node and evict non-critical pods to stop noisy neighbors from causing cascade. I'll prepare cordon + drain steps.

eng-runtime-jordan: Noted — we've been rolling a new quantized variant to that pool earlier (redwood-large-8q). If it's hitting a kernel regression we should route traffic to fallbacks (redwood-large-16) and lower concurrency for warm pools.

sre-maya: Plan (short): 1) Cordon gpu-node-12 2) Evict batch/low-priority pods 3) Force-evict the inference pod if it doesn't terminate 4) Update routing to fallback model variant 5) Monitor 15m.

sre-maya: Applying commands now:
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-node-12
kubectl -n batch delete pod -l job=preprocessing --grace-period=0 --force || true
kubectl -n inference drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force --grace-period=30 || true
```

oncall-alex: Eviction started. Found OOM traces in inference logs: "CUDA out of memory when allocating 12.34GiB" and repeated attempts to allocate KV cache for sequences >2048.

eng-runtime-jordan: That aligns with a recent increase in max_context for some customers ("libra-app" ramped to 4096). We should temporarily cap max_sequence for that model on this pool and route long-context requests to dedicated or smaller model. I'll push a routing change.

eng-runtime-jordan: Running gateway route update (hot):
```bash
# route fallback to redwood-large-16 on pool prod-low-latency when mem pressure > 90%
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/routes/update \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer **REDACTED**' \
  -d '{"pool":"inference-pool-prod","condition":"gpu_mem>90","fallback":"redwood-large-16"}'
```

oncall-alex: Customer impact: Observed ~150 5xx responses in last 10m for customer "libra-app" (hosted on dedicated route through this pool). Latency spikes to 2.8s p95 from baseline 200ms for small requests. Marking customer impact pending. Notifying customer-success if this escalates.

sre-maya: After cordon/drain the offending pod eviction succeeded. Memory pressure dropped from 97% -> 72% in ~5m. GPU processes leftover from inference-redwood-5 were terminated.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD12345 acknowledged by oncall-alex at 1754109999. Next escalation in 8 minutes if status not updated.

eng-runtime-jordan: To reduce recurrence, I've deployed a temporary policy change: cap_context=2048 for redwood-large-8q on inference-pool-prod and lowered max_concurrency from 8 -> 4. Also enabled fallback routing for >2048 sequences.

oncall-alex: Observing traffic now. Error rate for libra-app trending down to near baseline; 5xx count decreased to 12 in last 10m. Good.

infra-ops-lee: Can we check node-level ECC/driver messages? Shared note: recent driver patch rolled last week on this cluster (nv_driver 525.78). If OOMs persist could be either driver-level page fragmentation or kernel regression in allocator. Logging support ticket with cloud provider if we see repeated OOMs.

sre-maya: Agreed. For now mitigation stands. I'll keep node cordoned and schedule a maintenance to repro and repro with synthetic load.

oncall-alex: Status update for PD: Mitigated — memory pressure reduced after draining node and routing fallback. Impact: transient 5xxs for one customer (libra-app), ~150 errors over 10m window, now reduced to single digits. No data loss or secret exfiltration.

sre-maya: Post-action items: - Run reproducer on staging with same nv driver and quantized model - Re-evaluate max_context default and add guardrails for pool assignment - Add alert to detect rapid increase in max_sequence requests per pool - Consider auto-fallback sooner in routing logic

eng-runtime-jordan: I've filed issue: https://go.redwood/issues/RI-4287 "GPU OOM under high max_context on prod pool" with logs and stack traces. Assigning to runtime team for follow-up.

oncall-alex: Handing off monitoring to infra-ops-lee for overnight. Will keep PD incident open but acknowledged/resolved status updated.

infra-ops-lee: Taking over monitoring. I'll keep node cordoned and watch metrics for 1h; will uncordon only when stable for 30m. Ping me if it flares back up.

incident-bot: This thread has been tagged P1 -> mitigated by oncall-alex, handoff to infra-ops-lee. PD12345 state: acknowledged -> resolved (manual) at 1754110280 :white_check_mark:

oncall-alex: Thanks team. Filing a short blameless blurb for postmortem and linking runbook.

sre-maya: tl;dr: transient CUDA OOM tied to larger-than-typical context sizes + new quantized variant; mitigated by node drain + fallback routing + concurrency cap. Follow-ups assigned.

eng-runtime-jordan: Adding note: consider adding per-customer soft-limits and a preflight check at gateway that rejects requests which would allocate >X GiB on that model variant to avoid repeated OOM churn.

oncall-alex: Closing thread here, continuing tracking in issue RI-4287. :thumbsup:
